practical_guide.title: Getting a BSN

short_summary.text: A BSN is assigned through registration: residents use the municipal BRP route, while eligible non-residents use an RNI desk. It is normally not a separate BSN application.

who_this_is_for.text: Use this guide if you are moving to the Netherlands, staying for a short period, or need to check whether a BSN was already assigned during an earlier stay.

when_you_need_it.text: Choose the route before booking: living in the Netherlands for more than four months normally means resident BRP registration; living abroad or staying for less than four months points to RNI registration.

jurisdiction.note: The resident/non-resident split is national; municipalities and RNI desks execute registration and set operational appointment requirements.

prerequisites.text: Determine whether you will live in the Netherlands for more than four months or remain a non-resident/short-stay visitor.
If you previously lived, worked or studied in the Netherlands, check whether you already have a BSN before starting a new registration.

required_documents.text: Bring a valid identity document. The responsible municipality or RNI desk may request additional identity, lawful-residence, address or civil-status evidence for your route.
For an RNI registration of a child under 16, the official route also requires the child's identity document and evidence of parentage; foreign documents may need legalisation or translation.

estimated_time.note: There is no universal processing time. Appointment availability and any identity or lawful-residence investigation can change the timing.

estimated_cost.note: Travel, translation or legalisation can still create costs; this draft does not claim a universal total.

numbered_steps.title: Choose BRP or RNI
numbered_steps.body: Use expected residence duration and where you live to select the resident BRP route or the non-resident RNI route.

numbered_steps.title: Check for an existing BSN
numbered_steps.body: If you had an earlier Dutch connection, follow the official check route rather than trying to obtain a second number.

numbered_steps.title: Register as a resident
numbered_steps.body: If you will live in the Netherlands for more than four months, register with the municipality where you live. The national page says a newly arrived resident should do this within five days of arrival.

numbered_steps.title: Use an eligible RNI desk
numbered_steps.body: If you live abroad or will stay for less than four months, check the current RNI desk eligibility and appointment instructions before travelling to a desk.

numbered_steps.title: Keep the assigned number securely
numbered_steps.body: The BSN is assigned as a result of BRP or RNI registration and is used for contacts with Dutch public services.

warnings.text: Do not treat the BSN as a standalone commercial product or a separate ordinary application; first choose the correct registration route.
Do not copy one municipality's appointment or document list to another municipality; operational requirements vary.

common_mistakes.text: Booking an RNI desk while actually becoming a resident for more than four months.
Trying to obtain a new BSN without checking whether an earlier Dutch stay already produced one.

tips.text: Open the current page of your municipality or selected RNI desk immediately before booking and travelling.
For resident registration, accompanying partners and children who moved with you should attend as described by the national route.

checklist.text: I selected BRP or RNI based on my actual residence situation.
I checked the responsible office's current identity and supporting-document requirements.
I checked whether I may already have a BSN.

faqs.question: What is a BSN?
faqs.answer: It is a unique personal number assigned to people registered in the BRP, including through the relevant resident or non-resident registration route.

faqs.question: Where do I get a BSN?
faqs.answer: Residents receive it through municipal BRP registration. Eligible non-residents receive it through RNI registration. Limited government-organisation routes exist only for specified situations.

faqs.question: Do I need a new BSN after returning?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. If you previously lived, worked or studied in the Netherlands, first check whether a BSN was already assigned.

emergency_information.text: There is no national emergency BSN route in these sources. If a deadline is close, contact the responsible municipality or RNI desk and explain the specific deadline.

sections.title: Local variation
sections.body: Municipal appointment channels, desk availability and supporting-document checks are operational details. This national guide must link to the user's own municipality or eligible RNI desk.

sections.title: What comes next
sections.body: A BSN is used in government, healthcare and education workflows. DigiD is a separate digital identity process and is not created automatically by obtaining a BSN.

practical_guide.title: Finding and registering with a huisarts

short_summary.text: Find a nearby GP practice, ask whether it accepts new patients and register with your ID, BSN and insurance details. If you cannot find a practice, ask your insurer for help.

who_this_is_for.text: For people settled in the Netherlands who need a regular family doctor, including people whose first-choice practice is full or too far away.

when_you_need_it.text: Register after you are settled, before you need routine care. This guide is not a substitute for urgent or emergency medical triage.

jurisdiction.note: Insurance coverage rules are national, but practice capacity, distance and registration channels are local/provider-specific.

prerequisites.text: Use your place of residence to look for practices in your area; a practice may decline because it is full or you live too far away.
Have your health-insurance details available and check provider contracting if your policy restricts contracted care.

required_documents.text: Have your ID, BSN and health-insurance name and number available when registering.
For the first visit, bring available medical records and a current medication list.

estimated_time.note: No official national processing time or capacity guarantee exists; timing depends on local practice availability.

estimated_cost.value: GP care itself is covered by the basic package and exempt from the compulsory deductible
estimated_cost.note: Medicines, external tests, referred care and non-contracted-provider consequences may still create costs under the policy.

numbered_steps.title: Search near your home
numbered_steps.body: Search for GP or huisarts together with your place of residence and identify practices close enough for local care.

numbered_steps.title: Check acceptance and policy
numbered_steps.body: Ask the practice whether it accepts new patients and confirm any distance or insurance-contract issue before submitting details.

numbered_steps.title: Register
numbered_steps.body: Follow the practice's current online or in-person process and provide ID, BSN and health-insurance details.

numbered_steps.title: Transfer useful records
numbered_steps.body: Bring records and a medication list to the first visit. If changing Dutch GPs, authorise the previous GP to send the record to the new practice.

numbered_steps.title: Escalate a failed search
numbered_steps.body: If practices are full or waits are excessive, ask your health insurer for help or care mediation.

warnings.text: Free choice does not guarantee acceptance; practices may be full, too far away or incompatible with policy contracting.
Do not assume every service ordered by a GP is deductible-free; external tests, medicines and referred care may use the deductible.

common_mistakes.text: Waiting until routine care is needed before beginning the local registration search.
Treating one refusal as proof that no help is available instead of asking the insurer for mediation.

tips.text: Register with a nearby pharmacy so the practice knows where to send prescriptions.
Keep a concise current medication list ready for the first appointment.

checklist.text: I searched near my actual place of residence and checked whether the practice accepts patients.
I have ID, BSN and health-insurance details ready.
I prepared relevant records and a medication list.

faqs.question: Is registering with a GP mandatory?
faqs.answer: Government guidance describes registration as recommended rather than mandatory, so care is easier to access when needed.

faqs.question: What if every nearby GP is full?
faqs.answer: Ask your health insurer to help find a practice or provide care mediation when capacity or waiting time is the problem.

faqs.question: Does GP care use the compulsory deductible?
faqs.answer: GP care itself is in the basic package and exempt from the compulsory deductible, but external tests, medicines and referred care may not be.

emergency_information.text: For immediate danger or a serious injury needing prompt medical attention, call 112. Do not wait for ordinary GP registration.

sections.title: Local variation
sections.body: Actual practices, registration forms, capacity and out-of-hours contacts vary by area. The public guide needs a city-aware handoff rather than a single national form.

sections.title: If registration fails
sections.body: Record which practices you contacted, then ask the insurer for help. Care mediation is the official escalation when availability or waiting time is excessive.

practical_guide.title: Renting a home safely

short_summary.text: Once you find a possible home, check its rental sector and points, the basic rent and service costs, the deposit, any mediation fee, local permit rules and the written tenancy agreement before committing.

who_this_is_for.text: For people comparing or entering a Dutch tenancy, including workers whose employer also arranges accommodation.

when_you_need_it.text: Use the checks before paying a deposit or signing, and use the escalation section if the landlord later breaches rent, service-cost, deposit or conduct rules.

jurisdiction.note: National tenancy rules apply, while rental permits, allocation rules and municipal reporting routes can vary by city.

prerequisites.text: Have the address, proposed basic rent, service costs, deposit, contract date and whether the home is self-contained or shared.
Check whether the municipality requires a rental or housing permit for this address and household.

required_documents.text: Obtain the written tenancy agreement and the landlord's written information about use, access, repair, contacts, deposit and service costs.
Record the condition of the home at the start and keep the agreed property-condition record with the contract.
Keep evidence of the deposit, rent, service-cost and any agency payments.

estimated_time.note: There is no official national search or approval time. Permit, allocation and landlord processes vary locally.

estimated_cost.value: Rent, actual service costs and any lawful deposit
estimated_cost.note: For agreements dated 1 July 2023 or later, the current government plan caps the deposit at two months' basic rent. Recheck current annual rent thresholds before publication.

numbered_steps.title: Check local eligibility
numbered_steps.body: Open the municipality's current housing pages and verify whether this address or tenancy needs a permit or follows local allocation rules.

numbered_steps.title: Check sector and rent
numbered_steps.body: Use the official Rent Check for a self-contained or shared home and identify whether social, midprice or private-sector rules apply.

numbered_steps.title: Separate every cost
numbered_steps.body: Separate basic rent, actual service costs, utilities, deposit and any mediation fee; do not accept one unexplained total.

numbered_steps.title: Read the written agreement
numbered_steps.body: Check the core terms, written landlord information and starting condition of the property before signing or moving in.

numbered_steps.title: Check possible housing benefit
numbered_steps.body: Use the official Dienst Toeslagen route to check possible eligibility; do not assume the property or household qualifies.

numbered_steps.title: Use the correct dispute route
numbered_steps.body: First document the issue and contact the landlord. Depending on the issue and sector, use the Huurcommissie, municipal reporting office or district court route described by the official plan.

warnings.text: The two-month deposit rule cited here applies to tenancy agreements dated 1 July 2023 or later; do not reuse it for older contracts without review.
An agency acting for the landlord cannot also charge the tenant mediation fees; a separately instructed tenant agent is a different case.
For covered European labour migrants with employer-provided housing, agreements dated 1 July 2023 or later must separate the tenancy from the employment contract.

common_mistakes.text: Comparing only one total price without separating basic rent, service costs, utilities and deposit.
Relying on verbal promises that are absent from the written tenancy information.
Assuming Den Haag or another municipality uses the same permit and allocation rules as every other city.

tips.text: Run the official Rent Check before committing and save the result with the listing and contract.
Create a dated condition record at move-in so later damage discussions can be compared with the starting state.

checklist.text: I checked the municipality's current permit or allocation rules for this address.
I separated basic rent, service costs, utilities, deposit and agency fees.
I have a written agreement, landlord information and starting-condition record.
I kept receipts and correspondence for every payment and promise.

faqs.question: How large can the deposit be?
faqs.answer: For tenancy agreements dated 1 July 2023 or later, the current Government.nl plan says a maximum of two months' basic rent. Older agreements require separate review.

faqs.question: Can the rental agent charge both parties?
faqs.answer: An agent acting for the landlord cannot also charge the tenant mediation fees. If the tenant independently instructed an agent, that is treated differently.

faqs.question: Where do I report a landlord problem?
faqs.answer: The route depends on the issue and rental sector. The official plan routes relevant cases to the landlord, Huurcommissie, municipal reporting office or district court.

emergency_information.text: This guide does not establish an emergency gas, fire or structural-safety procedure. Use the relevant emergency service for immediate danger and do not wait for a tenancy dispute route.

sections.title: Local variation
sections.body: Den Haag and other municipalities may add rental permits, allocation conditions or local reporting routes. Link to the municipality for the exact address rather than presenting one city as national law.

sections.title: Related topics
sections.body: Housing benefit, defect repair, registration at the address and employer-provided accommodation are separate journeys that need their own eligibility and evidence checks.

practical_guide.title: Finding work in the Netherlands

short_summary.text: First verify whether you can work under your nationality and residence route, then use UWV/EURES tools to prepare a CV, search vacancies and keep evidence required by any applicable benefit rules.

who_this_is_for.text: For jobseekers in the Netherlands, including EU/EEA/Swiss jobseekers and non-EEA residents who must first check their work-authorisation route.

when_you_need_it.text: Use this before applying or accepting work, especially when nationality, residence status, an unemployment benefit or an agency relationship may change the route.

jurisdiction.note: Work authorisation and UWV services are national; vacancy availability remains market- and location-specific.

prerequisites.text: Check whether you can work without a permit or whether the employer/route needs a TWV or GVVA; exceptions are status-specific.
If you receive an unemployment benefit or bring a PD U2 from another eligible country, check the specific UWV registration and activity rules for that route.

required_documents.text: Prepare a current CV for the UWV Work Folder or vacancy applications.
Keep the residence/work-authorisation evidence relevant to your route; do not assume one permit rule applies to all nationalities.
If UWV benefit rules require job-search activities, retain the evidence specified for those activities.

estimated_time.note: The official sources provide no universal time to find a job or receive an offer.

estimated_cost.note: No universal job-search cost is supported; permits, travel, recognition or training can be route-specific.

numbered_steps.title: Verify the right-to-work route
numbered_steps.body: Separate Dutch/EEA/Swiss access from non-EEA and exception routes, then follow the relevant current government or IND/UWV instructions.

numbered_steps.title: Prepare a job profile
numbered_steps.body: Create a current CV and the information needed to use the UWV Work Folder or apply directly to vacancies.

numbered_steps.title: Search official channels
numbered_steps.body: Use UWV and, where relevant, EURES services to search vacancies and access job-search support.

numbered_steps.title: Follow only applicable benefit rules
numbered_steps.body: If you receive a benefit, follow the UWV activity and evidence requirements for your case; do not apply those duties to every jobseeker.

numbered_steps.title: Review the offer and contract
numbered_steps.body: Before starting, verify the employer, work authorisation and written employment terms, then use the separate employment-contract guide.

warnings.text: Do not generalise EEA/Swiss work access to non-EEA nationals; permits and exceptions depend on the person's status and job.
The seven-day PD U2 registration rule applies to the specified cross-border benefit route, not to every jobseeker.

common_mistakes.text: Applying widely before confirming whether the intended job and residence status allow work.
Treating benefit-specific job-search reporting duties as universal employment law.

tips.text: Use EURES support when your job-search route is within the EU/EEA or Switzerland.
Keep the Work Folder profile and CV current if you use UWV services.

checklist.text: I verified my exact work-authorisation route.
My CV and job profile are current.
I know whether any UWV benefit reporting duties actually apply to me.

faqs.question: Do I need a work permit?
faqs.answer: Dutch, EEA and Swiss nationals generally do not. Non-EEA routes commonly require a TWV or GVVA unless a specific exception applies; verify the exact status before work starts.

faqs.question: Where can I search for work?
faqs.answer: UWV provides job-search portals and coordinates EURES support in the Netherlands for eligible European routes.

faqs.question: How long does finding work take?
faqs.answer: The official sources do not provide a universal duration or guarantee. It depends on the role, location, qualifications, permission route and labour market.

emergency_information.text: A job-search problem is not an emergency route. If an employer is withholding wages or making unlawful deductions, use the official labour-reporting routes linked by WorkinNL rather than delaying for a general job-search guide.

sections.title: Local variation
sections.body: The legal route is national, but jobs and language requirements vary by sector and city. A Leiden query should boost Leiden vacancies or services without hiding national work-authorisation guidance.

sections.title: Related checks
sections.body: An offer still requires a contract, wage and payslip review. Work authorisation does not prove that every contract term is correct.

practical_guide.title: Understanding a Dutch employment contract

short_summary.text: Check the written core terms, whether the job is fixed-term or permanent, the applicable collective agreement, gross wage and deductions, and compare the first payslip with the agreement.

who_this_is_for.text: For employees reviewing an offer, a newly started job or a payslip against the promised Dutch employment terms.

when_you_need_it.text: Use it before signing and again after work starts, because specified information is due in writing within one week and other information within one month.

jurisdiction.note: Employment-contract rules are national; the applicable CAO and sector terms vary by employer and role.

prerequisites.text: Have the offer or employment agreement and identify the employer, role, start date, hours and proposed gross wage.
Ask which CAO, if any, applies to the employer and role.

required_documents.text: Keep the employment agreement and every written statement of employment terms supplied by the employer.
Keep or link the current applicable CAO when one applies.
Keep the first payslip and later payslips when pay or tax information changes.

estimated_time.value: Core written information within one week; specified additional information within one month after employment starts
estimated_time.note: These are employer information deadlines, not a guarantee for resolving a contract dispute.

estimated_cost.note: Reading and checking the documents has no universal official fee; professional advice or proceedings can cost money.

numbered_steps.title: Check the core terms
numbered_steps.body: Confirm employer and employee details, place of work, role, start date, hours, wage and payment timing in the written information.

numbered_steps.title: Identify the contract type
numbered_steps.body: Determine whether the contract is fixed-term or permanent and whether early termination is expressly possible for a fixed term.

numbered_steps.title: Check the CAO
numbered_steps.body: Identify any applicable collective agreement and compare its binding terms with the individual contract.

numbered_steps.title: Check wage and deductions
numbered_steps.body: Separate gross and net wage, hours, holiday pay and every deduction; fines are not an allowed wage deduction under the cited WorkinNL guidance.

numbered_steps.title: Compare the first payslip
numbered_steps.body: Compare the hours, contract type, gross wage, tax, contributions and net payment on the payslip with the written terms.

warnings.text: An oral employment contract can exist, but Rijksoverheid advises recording the agreement in writing; do not rely on memory for disputed terms.
Do not review the individual contract without checking an applicable CAO, which can take priority under the official rules.
This draft does not decide whether a probation, dismissal, notice, non-compete, agency or zero-hours clause is lawful in an individual case.

common_mistakes.text: Comparing only the net payment and not the gross wage, hours, holiday pay, tax and deductions.
Assuming a fixed-term contract can always be ended early without checking the agreement.

tips.text: Keep dated copies of the signed agreement, written terms, CAO and payslips outside the employer's system.
Ask the employer to answer unclear terms in writing before signing or before the applicable information deadline.

checklist.text: I can identify the employer, role, start date, hours, gross wage and payment schedule.
I know whether the contract is fixed-term or permanent and whether a CAO applies.
I compared the first payslip and deductions with the written terms.

faqs.question: Must an employment contract be written?
faqs.answer: An oral contract can exist, but the employer must provide specified employment information in writing and Rijksoverheid advises recording the agreement in writing.

faqs.question: What is the main fixed-term difference?
faqs.answer: A fixed term normally ends automatically and usually cannot be ended early unless that possibility was agreed; a permanent contract continues until properly ended.

faqs.question: Why must I check the CAO?
faqs.answer: An applicable CAO can take priority over the individual employment agreement under the official collective-agreement rules.

emergency_information.text: If wages appear below the applicable minimum or unlawful deductions are made, use the official reporting routes linked by WorkinNL and preserve the contract and payslips as evidence.

sections.title: If the documents disagree
sections.body: Mark each difference between the offer, contract, CAO, hours worked and payslip. Ask for a written correction and obtain qualified advice before accepting a waiver or signing a replacement document.

sections.title: Related topics
sections.body: Work permission, dismissal, sickness, agency work and housing deductions are separate branches and should not be inferred from this general contract review.

practical_guide.title: Registering a child at a Dutch school

short_summary.text: Choose the primary or secondary route, check municipal allocation and school capacity, ask about needed support, then register with the child's BSN and identity evidence or the official no-BSN route.

who_this_is_for.text: For parents or guardians registering a child for Dutch primary or secondary education, including families who have just moved municipality or whose child needs extra support.

when_you_need_it.text: Primary registration can begin once a child is three; primary education can start at four and is compulsory from five. Secondary registration follows the current central-registration rules, while a move can allow registration during the year.

jurisdiction.note: National education rules apply, while municipalities and school boards may use local allocation, catchment, ranking or lottery arrangements.

prerequisites.text: Identify whether the child needs primary or secondary education and, for secondary school, obtain the primary-school advice where applicable.
Check the municipality and school websites for local catchment, allocation, lottery, capacity and registration arrangements.
Tell the school about extra support needs and ask how its duty of care will be applied if it cannot provide the needed support itself.

required_documents.text: Provide the child's BSN and proof of identity. The primary-school page accepts a birth certificate, passport or proof of identity for this purpose.
When transferring from another school, bring the old school's certificate or proof of deregistration.
For secondary admission, have the primary school's definitive school advice where that transition route applies.

estimated_time.note: Capacity, waiting lists, lotteries and local procedures vary. The current secondary page gives a 25–31 March central week, but the date must be rechecked for the relevant year.

estimated_cost.note: These registration sources do not provide one universal total for school-related costs.

numbered_steps.title: Choose primary or secondary
numbered_steps.body: Use the child's age, current school stage and school advice to select the correct registration route.

numbered_steps.title: Check Groningen or your municipality
numbered_steps.body: Review the local school-allocation rules, catchment areas, lotteries and newcomer support instead of assuming one national application form.

numbered_steps.title: Ask schools about capacity and support
numbered_steps.body: Check available places, waiting-list rules and whether the school can provide the child's required support.

numbered_steps.title: Register with evidence
numbered_steps.body: Submit the child's BSN and identity evidence, plus school advice or old-school deregistration evidence when the route requires them.

numbered_steps.title: Use the no-BSN route if needed
numbered_steps.body: For secondary registration, the official page says the school can issue a temporary education number when the child has no BSN; give the school the BSN after BRP registration.

numbered_steps.title: Confirm placement
numbered_steps.body: Keep the school's registration or placement confirmation and follow any stated next steps, waiting-list process or suitable-place route.

warnings.text: Do not reuse the stated secondary central-registration dates without checking the current school year and local process.
Registration does not guarantee the first-choice school has space; waiting lists, lotteries and school-board decisions can apply.
Do not present Groningen's local arrangements as national rules or another municipality's process.

common_mistakes.text: Relying on one preferred school without checking capacity, waiting lists or permitted multiple registrations.
Waiting until after admission to disclose support needs that the school must assess.

tips.text: Use school open days and school websites to compare the programme, support and current registration route.
If moving house requires a new secondary school, the national page says registration can occur during the year.

checklist.text: I selected the correct primary or secondary route.
I checked the current municipality and school-board allocation rules.
I prepared BSN/identity, old-school and school-advice evidence as applicable.

faqs.answer: A waiting list, lottery or alternative-school route may apply. Check the municipality and school-board rules and ask about another suitable place, especially when support is needed.

short_summary.text: For a mobile subscription, compare network coverage, data and minutes, total and out-of-bundle costs, contract duration, cancellation costs and the readable contract summary before agreeing.

who_this_is_for.text: For people choosing or switching a Dutch mobile subscription and anyone deciding whether the contract terms fit a short or long stay.

when_you_need_it.text: Use this before buying a SIM with a subscription, porting a number or cancelling an existing telecom contract.

jurisdiction.note: Consumer contract rules are national; actual network coverage and provider onboarding are provider- and location-specific.

prerequisites.text: Estimate the minutes, data, international use and contract duration you actually need.
Check each candidate provider's current coverage map at home, work or study locations such as Maastricht.
If switching, check whether the current subscription can be cancelled without an early-termination charge.

required_documents.text: Keep the readable contract summary showing product characteristics, duration, fixed and usage costs and cancellation costs.
Keep the current contract and cancellation confirmation when switching or porting a number.
Check the provider's own current onboarding requirements; the ACM sources do not establish one universal identity or payment-document list.

estimated_time.note: Activation, number porting and switching time are provider-specific; the ACM sources do not give one universal duration.

estimated_cost.value: Subscription, one-off, out-of-bundle, roaming and possible cancellation costs
estimated_cost.note: Compare the provider's current contract summary and tariff pages; ACM does not set provider prices.

numbered_steps.title: Define the real need
numbered_steps.body: Estimate monthly data and calls, international use, desired flexibility and whether a device is included.

numbered_steps.title: Check coverage
numbered_steps.body: Compare provider coverage maps for Maastricht and the exact places where the phone will be used; advertised maximum speed can differ from actual speed.

numbered_steps.title: Compare total cost
numbered_steps.body: Compare monthly and one-off prices, out-of-bundle rates, roaming, rounding, data caps, duration and cancellation costs.

numbered_steps.title: Read the contract summary
numbered_steps.body: Do not accept based only on an advert; retain the readable summary of the main product and contract properties.

numbered_steps.title: Plan switching and number porting
numbered_steps.body: Check the current contract's end and cancellation terms; the new provider can arrange number retention and often the switch.

numbered_steps.title: Use cancellation rights correctly
numbered_steps.body: For a subscription concluded online, by phone or on the street, ACM states a 14-day cooling-off period. After a fixed term, cancellation is normally free with at most one month's notice.

warnings.text: The official source supports subscription comparison; it does not establish one national prepaid/eSIM activation or ID rule.
Out-of-bundle and non-EU roaming costs can be much higher than the headline monthly price.
Cancelling during a fixed term can create remaining-term or device costs; read the individual contract.

common_mistakes.text: Choosing only by the headline monthly price without checking one-off, out-of-bundle, roaming and cancellation costs.
Assuming national marketing claims prove good coverage at the exact home or workplace.

tips.text: Consider a plan with usage alerts or a data cap to reduce unexpected bills.
Request and keep written cancellation confirmation so a later dispute can be evidenced.

faqs.answer: After the fixed term, a telecom subscription can normally be cancelled free at any time with a notice period of no more than one month. During the fixed term, contract or device costs may remain.

faqs.question: Can I keep my mobile number?
faqs.answer: The ACM page says the new provider arranges number retention when switching; check its operational requirements before ordering.

practical_guide.title: Handling a parking or traffic fine

short_summary.text: First identify the issuer and letter type: an Utrecht parking-tax assessment follows the BghU municipal route, while a CJIB letter code M follows the national traffic-fine route. The deadlines, payment effect and appeal recipient differ.

who_this_is_for.text: For a vehicle owner, driver or lease-car user who received an Utrecht parking-tax assessment or a CJIB traffic-fine letter and needs the correct official route.

when_you_need_it.text: Use the guide immediately after receiving the notice so you can classify it, preserve evidence and meet the applicable six-week objection or appeal deadline.

jurisdiction.note: Utrecht parking tax is handled through Utrecht/BghU; CJIB letter-code-M traffic fines use the national Public Prosecution Service route.

prerequisites.text: Read the heading, issuer and letter code. 'Naheffingsaanslag parkeerbelasting' indicates the municipal parking-tax branch; CJIB letter code M indicates a traffic fine.
Record the notice date and the payment, objection or appeal deadline before taking action.

required_documents.text: Keep the complete notice, envelope and payment details; use the notice reference in every action.
Keep relevant parking receipts, app confirmations, permit data, photographs of signs/location and other evidence supporting the objection.

A written BghU objection lists the vehicle owner's name, address, phone, BSN, notice date/time, registration plate, relevant permit/card copies, reasons and signature; lease-car cases require the stated lease evidence.
A CJIB M appeal letter lists name, address, residence, date and place of birth, reasons, IBAN, letter date and signature, with a copy of the fine notice.

estimated_time.value: Object or appeal within six weeks
estimated_time.note: CJIB says the Public Prosecution Service decision letter may take up to sixteen weeks. Municipal handling time is not stated as one fixed value here.

estimated_cost.value: Utrecht parking-tax assessment: hourly tariff plus a €78.80 surcharge on the checked 2026-08-05 page
estimated_cost.note: CJIB fine amounts vary by notice; unpaid CJIB M fines increase at the first and second reminders. Recheck all current amounts before publication.

numbered_steps.title: Classify the notice
numbered_steps.body: Separate an Utrecht/BghU parking-tax assessment from a CJIB letter-code-M traffic fine. Do not send one branch's objection to the other authority.

numbered_steps.title: Verify the facts
numbered_steps.body: Check number plate, location, date/time, paid-parking proof, permit details and the stated offence or tax basis against your records.

numbered_steps.title: Preserve evidence
numbered_steps.body: Save the notice, receipts, app records, photos, permit data and any lease or authorisation documents before systems or signage change.

numbered_steps.title: Use BghU for Utrecht parking tax
numbered_steps.body: Pay or object through the current BghU route. BghU says an objection can be submitted within six weeks and that payment deferral is granted after receipt of the objection.

numbered_steps.title: Use the CJIB M appeal route
numbered_steps.body: Send the complete appeal to the Public Prosecution Service within six weeks. CJIB says not to pay the outstanding amount while that appeal is pending.

numbered_steps.title: Track the decision
numbered_steps.body: Keep proof of submission and all correspondence. Follow the next route stated in the authority's decision rather than repeating the original objection.

warnings.text: A municipal parking-tax assessment is not the same as every traffic fine; the issuer, payment effect and appeal recipient differ.
For a CJIB M appeal, the official page says not to pay while the appeal is pending. Do not transfer that instruction automatically to a municipal assessment.
Ignoring a CJIB M fine can trigger reminders that increase the payable amount.

common_mistakes.text: Sending an Utrecht parking-tax objection to CJIB or a CJIB M appeal to BghU.
Waiting for more information while the six-week deadline expires instead of preserving evidence and following the stated route.
Submitting a written BghU or CJIB appeal without the required identifying details and signature.

tips.text: Save a PDF or screenshot of the completed online submission and the confirmation reference.
When a CJIB camera photo exists, use the official request route before finalising factual grounds for an appeal.

checklist.text: I identified the issuer and whether this is parking tax or a CJIB M traffic fine.
I recorded the notice date and deadline.
I saved the notice, payment/permit evidence and relevant photos.
I kept proof of payment, objection or appeal submission.

faqs.question: What does an Utrecht parking assessment cost?
faqs.answer: On the page checked 5 August 2026, Utrecht states the unpaid hourly parking tariff plus a €78.80 enforcement surcharge. Recheck the current page before acting.

faqs.question: How long do I have to object?
faqs.answer: The current BghU parking-tax and CJIB M routes both state six weeks, measured from the date specified by each route. Confirm the date on the actual notice.

faqs.question: Should I pay while objecting?
faqs.answer: For a CJIB M appeal, CJIB says not to pay while the appeal is pending. BghU states it grants payment deferral after receiving a parking-tax objection. Follow the correct issuer's instructions.

emergency_information.text: A fine is deadline-sensitive but not an emergency-service matter. Act promptly, preserve evidence and use only the issuer's current official contact route.

sections.title: Local variation
sections.body: The Utrecht/BghU branch applies to Utrecht parking tax. Another municipality can use a different tax authority, surcharge and objection portal, so resolve the issuer from the notice.

sections.title: CJIB traffic-fine branch
sections.body: A letter code M is enforced nationally by CJIB. The first notice has an eight-week payment period, while an appeal to the Public Prosecution Service must be made within six weeks.
